title: App Builder Visual Candidate Set
description: Several genuinely different visual directions over ONE frozen product truth, and the record of which one was promoted. The frozen truth is stated once for the set rather than per candidate, because candidates are only comparable if they say the same thing. Exactly one candidate may reach 'promoted'; a rejected candidate keeps its evidence and its reason here and never becomes a second workspace the project has to maintain. Promotion is a recorded decision with a deterministic gate status and a named reviewer, not an ad hoc choice.

frozenTruth.description: What every candidate in this set shares. A candidate that regenerated any of it is not a visual candidate, and the composer transform proves the sharing rather than asserting it.

knowledgePackHash.description: Null is a fact rather than a gap: a project replayed from an approved intake bundle has an approved manifest and no ingested material. `knowledgeSource` says which case this is, so a reviewer never has to guess whether a hash went missing.

renderer.description: The renderer every candidate in this set was built through, agreed across the set rather than declared for it. A direction changes presentation and never capability, so a set whose candidates disagree here is refused at generation.

assetReadiness.description: Whether the approved inventory can support an imagery-led direction. Resolved before directions are selected, so 'no publishable imagery' selects a typography-led direction rather than breaking an imagery-led one.

businessProfile.description: What sort of visual problem this business presents, derived from approved intake. Selection used to see only the project type and the asset inventory, so two marketing sites with no photography were indistinguishable and received the same three directions. Every signal names the field it was read from and why, because this informs a design decision a person is entitled to disagree with and an opaque score cannot be argued with. It is not a source of truth: it invents no fact, alters no service, route, content or right, and only decides which treatment presents what is already approved.

directionFit.description: How well each chosen direction suits this business, and which derived signals it matched. A score of zero is a real answer: the direction was eligible and nothing about this business argued for it, which is what a tie-break resolved on registry order looks like.

truthReadiness.description: What this set's product truth is actually made of. A manifest declaring sources is not the same as a run having read them, and the difference decides whether candidates may be generated at all: material content left unread starves the truth and is refused, while a research location nobody read and an approved asset whose bytes never arrived are recorded gaps rather than defects. Present so a reviewer judging these candidates knows whether they are looking at ingested source-backed truth or owner-approved intake with gaps, and never reads the second as the first.

diversity.description: The deterministic proof that this set is a choice rather than one build in several colours. Token values are deliberately absent from the signature the check reads.

refusedDirections.description: Directions the registry offered that this project may not present by, with the reason. A direction refused for lack of publishable photography is an art-direction decision and is recorded as one.

setOutcome.description: What was decided about the set as a whole. Promotion answers 'which of these'; it cannot answer 'none of these', and a system whose only recordable outcome is a winner ships the least bad candidate by default. 'rework-required' keeps the set open for one bounded revision; 'rejected' closes it with no product change, which is a legitimate professional conclusion.

reworkPlans.description: The bounded revisions this set has asked for. Each names the candidate it revises, the criteria that failed, the axis changes requested and the iteration it belongs to, so a revised candidate can always be traced to the verdict that asked for it.

runtimeIdentity.description: Who acted, and what actually produced the act. `vendor` is load-bearing: independence is decided by comparing it, because a role name is chosen by the caller and the same model under a second label is the same opinion.

state.description: draft -> rendered -> deterministic-pass -> reviewed -> promoted, or -> rejected from any state after draft. A deterministic-blocked candidate can never reach promoted.

clamped.description: What restraintLevel cut from the declared plan, so a reviewer can tell a build that was asked to be quiet from one that was cut back.

referenceAdjustments.description: What an approved design reference changed about the direction's declared intent, and whether it was a preference or a refusal. Recorded beside `clamped` for the same reason: a reviewer looking at an unusual plan must be able to tell what asked for it.

reworkOverrides.description: The axis values a bounded rework pass asked this revision to differ by, flattened from its plan. Present only on a revised candidate.

signature.description: The structural identity of this candidate. Excludes every token, so two candidates that differ only in colour sign identically and the diversity check refuses them.

workspace.description: Where this candidate was built while it was being compared. Temporary by design: a rejected candidate's workspace is removed and only its evidence survives.

renderer.description: The renderer that produced this candidate, recorded per candidate so the set-level agreement is checkable rather than assumed.

portability.description: Proof, gathered before the review rather than at promotion, that this candidate is a repository somebody could be handed: it checked, it built, it emitted a servable artifact, and it declares no dependency on the factory that made it. A reviewer is about to be asked to judge the composition, and a screenshot says nothing about whether the thing behind it stands up. Recorded rather than merely performed, because a check nobody can see is indistinguishable from a check nobody ran.

install.description: How this workspace got its dependency tree. A set installs once and shares it across byte-identical package.json files, so `clean` and `shared-from-sibling` are different claims and only the first was proven directly here.

steps.description: The repository's own verification scripts, run the way its own CI would run them.

factoryIndependence.description: Whether the generated repository can live outside the factory. A factory-scoped package or a filesystem-local specifier installs here and nowhere else.

artifact.description: What the production build emitted. A zero exit code is not the same as having shipped something, and a build that succeeds and writes nothing would otherwise be photographed as a blank page with nothing saying why.

review.description: The independent verdict, with its criterion scores and whether they cleared the declared professional bar. A verdict with no scores cannot clear the bar, which is what stops 'looks fine to me' promoting a build.

iteration.description: 0 for a candidate the set was generated with; 1 or more for a revision produced by a bounded rework pass.

lineage.description: Where a revised candidate came from. A revision that cannot name its parent, the verdict that asked for it and the frozen truth it kept is not a revision; it is a second attempt pretending to be one.

reworkOwner.description: The role that owns fixing a failed candidate. Null unless the outcome is a rejection something can be done about.

gate.description: What the deterministic checks already settled. A violation blocks promotion outright; a warning lets a candidate reach review but the reviewer has to address it by rule; a recommendation never blocks anything.

mustAddress.description: Rule ids the visual review has to speak to. A review that ignores one is refused rather than accepted quietly.
